newsitem.title: CANADA: Fletcher Canada to take C$15 mln charge.
newsitem.headline: Fletcher Canada to take C$15 mln charge.

text.p: Fletcher Challenge Canada Ltd said Monday it will take an after-tax charge of C$15 million or C$0.12 a share in its second fiscal quarter ended December 31 to cover costs of a previously announced reorganization.
The provision amounts to C$25 million before taxes. Under the restructuring, the forest company will create "distinct and separate organizations for its paper and its pulp businesses."
Fletcher Canada is majority owned by New Zealand's Fletcher Challenge Ltd.
Fletcher said it plans to eliminate 285 jobs, or about 40 percent of its salaried workforce. The reorganization is expected to result in operating efficiencies and reduced overhead.
The company estimated the ongoing savings at C$25 million to C$30 million a year before taxes. The reorganization is to be completed by the end of calendar 1997.
About 40 percent of the departing workers are taking early retirement settlements while most others are eligible for severance packages.

Fletcher previously said it might decide to spin off its pulp operation as a separate entity, possibly through a public offering, but a company spokesman said no decision has been made. He said there was no firm timetable for a decision.
